text:
olivia: quick question — deploy-bot just auto-bumped a PR to v1.12.4 but it was only a prometheus scrape config change. should config-only still be a patch bump?

sam: we chatted about this before but no settled rule iirc. current deploybot heuristic: any change touches src/ or runbooks => bump patch, docs-only => skip. config lives in infra/ so it's fuzzy.

jia: my vote: config that affects runtime behavior (env vars, feature flags, autoscale) => patch. pure monitoring/observability tweaks => don’t bump. reduces churn.

mike: +1 for behavioral criteria. can we make deploy-bot check a list? e.g. if diff touches 'infra/runtime' or 'pkg/' => bump, else optional.

lena: operationally we want a short changelog for each patch release. If we skip bump, the change still lands to main — how will teams know? maybe require an 'ops: changelog' entry in PR if not bumping.

olivia: that seems reasonable. proposed ruleset:
- patch bump required if code changes that can change runtime outputs or client contract (handlers, models, CLI)
- optional for non-runtime infra (monitoring, dashboards) but must include 'ops: changelog' label to trigger release-note entry
- docs-only (README, ADRs) => no patch bump

sam: what about preserving buildmeta in tags? i.e. v1.12.4 vs v1.12.4+build.20260312.ab12cd

jia: i'd like to keep buildmeta in the git tag (not in semver number used by clients). canonical tag can be `v1.12.4+git.ab12cd` but our SDKs should resolve by the base semver v1.12.4. buildmeta helps traceability for ops.

mike: agree, but deploybot needs to decide when to keep buildmeta vs strip it for stable channels. maybe rule: for release branches we keep `vX.Y.Z` simple; for nightly/auto patches we append +build.<shortsha>.

deploy-bot: autoprunebot check: diff files changed: ["infra/monitoring/prom.yaml", "ops/alerts/README.md"]. heuristic: no src/ changes detected. suggested action: mark as "config-only-monitoring". decision required: bump_patch? false (requires ops: changelog to avoid silent change).

lena: deploy-bot +1 on suggested action. request author to add a short note in PR body that will be copied into the release notes if we skip bump. we can also aggregate such non-patch infra changes into monthly "observability" patch if teams want atomicity.

olivia: release note format proposed for these cases (single-line entries):
- [component] (infra) short summary — PR #1234 — @owner
Example:
- prometheus (infra) add scrape job for blackbox-exporter — PR #4321 — @olivia

sam: for real patch releases we require: a one-line summary + impact (none/minor/rollback risk) + test signal. e.g.
- api (runtime) fix token parsing regression — impact: minor, rollback-risk: low, test: e2e-auth

jia: also: pinning policy — we should avoid pinning minor/patch deps in patch releases unless necessary. pin (major.minor) for reproducible builds on dedicated infra, but let minor float for hosted to allow security fixes.

mike: tl;dr rules to implement in deploy-bot:
1) classify diffs (runtime / infra-behavioral / infra-monitoring / docs)
2) require label 'ops: changelog' for infra-monitoring if not bumping
3) attach buildmeta for auto-patches only (tag = vX.Y.Z+git.<sha>), keep plain tag for branch-promoted releases
4) release-note templates enforced by PR checklist

lena: approve. can someone open a tiny RFC to lock wording? I'll need it for the onboarding doc.

olivia: i'll draft RFC and a short deploy-bot config PR. will ping when ready. :thumbsup:
